# Consensus clustering {#sec-consensus}

**What it is.** Receptors that recognise the same epitope tend to be similar rather than
identical, and each clustering method captures similarity differently: GIANA (CDR3β geometry
plus V gene), GLIPH2 (shared CDR3β motifs) and TCRdist3 (biochemical distance over the CDR
loops), all per patient; on the single-cell VDJ+GEX route also CoNGA, whose hit clonotypes are
grouped by their gene-expression and TCR clusters. Two clonotypes are linked when at least
`--consensus_min_methods` methods (default 2) put them in the same cluster, and each connected
group is one consensus cluster.

**Receptor-only and receptor + expression methods.** CoNGA is the only method that uses both
the receptor (VDJ) and the cell's gene expression (GEX); GIANA, GLIPH2 and TCRdist3 use the
receptor sequence alone, and CoNGA only runs on the VDJ+GEX route. This helps interpret a
cluster by which methods support it:

- **Supported by the receptor-only methods alone**: the receptors are similar, a sequence-level
  prediction of shared specificity, whatever the cells' phenotype.
- **Supported by CoNGA as well**: the similar receptors also sit in cells with the same
  transcriptional programme. Two independent kinds of evidence agree, which makes a shared
  antigen-driven response much more likely; these are the strongest candidates.
- **Supported by CoNGA and only one receptor method**: the expression signal may be carrying
  the cluster; check whether it is an innate-like population (MAIT, iNKT), whose semi-invariant
  receptors cluster with a fixed phenotype without sharing a conventional antigen.

On the bulk and VDJ-only routes, consensus rests on receptor similarity only.

**Why it matters.** A cluster that independent definitions of similarity agree on is far less
likely to be an artefact of one method, so consensus clusters are the strongest candidates for
groups of receptors sharing a specificity, to test against known epitopes or follow over time.

**How to read it.** The bar chart ranks the largest consensus clusters by cells (clonotype rows
for bulk data); the table gives each cluster's patient, the methods that support it and the
cluster each method gave it. Clusters spanning several clonotypes and supported by three or
more methods are the most robust. Each method's own results are in the **Details: Patient**
report, and on the VDJ+GEX route the cell states of these clusters are in the GEX section below.

```{r}
#| label: consensus
if (!have(cons_clusters)) {
  note("Consensus clustering produced no clusters on this run.")
} else {
  save_table(cons_clusters, "master_consensus_clusters.tsv")
  d <- cons_clusters
  nc <- intersect(c("n_cells", "cells", "n"), names(d))
  cc <- intersect(c("consensus_cluster", "cluster"), names(d))
  if (!length(nc) || !length(cc)) itable(d, pageSize = 15) else {
    dd <- data.frame(cat = as.character(d[[cc[1]]]), val = as.numeric(d[[nc[1]]]))
    dd <- dd[order(-dd$val), , drop = FALSE]
    dd <- head(dd, params$top_n_clusters)
    dd$hover <- paste0("cluster ", dd$cat, "<br>", dd$val, " cells")
    hbar(dd, paste0("Top ", params$top_n_clusters, " consensus clusters"), "Cells", height = 560)
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: consensus-table
itable(cons_clusters, pageSize = 10)
```

# Reference tables

Every table rendered above is also written to `Master_Summary_Report/tables/` as TSV for
downstream use.

```{r}
#| label: written-tables
files <- list.files(file.path(params$outdir, "tables"), pattern = "\\.tsv$")
if (!length(files)) note("No tables were written.") else {
  itable(data.frame(table = sort(files), stringsAsFactors = FALSE), pageSize = 25)
}
```

# Session info

```{r}
#| label: session
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()),
           file.path(params$outdir, "sessionInfo.master_summary.txt"))
sessionInfo()
```
